case_title: Serologically proven West Nile encephalitis with delayed deep white-matter MRI abnormalities
source_title: A Case of West Nile Encephalitis That Develops into a Disease of Deep White Matter on MRI over a Two-Week Span

confirmatory_evidence: CSF West Nile IgM positive by ELISA
CSF West Nile IgG positive by ELISA
Aseptic lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis with elevated protein
Initial brain MRI normal, repeat MRI around hospital day 16 showed periventricular deep white-matter changes
case_quality.boundary_notes: This is West Nile encephalitis with delayed white-matter MRI evolution, not isolated viral meningitis or HSV/VZV encephalitis.

time_anchor.day0_definition: Hospital presentation with altered mental status, fever, headache, lumbar puncture, CT, and initial MRI

risk_context.source_text_value: Returned from Mexico three days before becoming ill.
Denied mosquito bites; absence of recalled bite is not exclusion evidence.

presentation_summary: 57-year-old woman presented with three days of altered mental status, fever, and posterior head/neck headache after recent travel from Mexico.
At evaluation she was lethargic and oriented to person only, without initial focal weakness, sensory loss, cranial nerve abnormality, seizure, or gait abnormality.
Initial CT and MRI brain showed no acute intracranial abnormality.
CSF showed WBC 127/uL with 85% lymphocytes, RBC 6/uL, protein 177 mg/dL, glucose 54 mg/dL, and positive West Nile CSF IgM and IgG.
EEG monitoring did not reveal seizures.
On hospital day 16, she became more lethargic and nursing staff noted facial droop and left-sided weakness; repeat MRI showed moderate periventricular white-matter changes.
She improved with supportive treatment and was discharged home alert, oriented, walking, and following commands.

observations.source_text_value: Presented with fever of three days duration.
Fever was documented but no numeric temperature was provided.
Headache localized to the back of the head and neck area, with obvious pain distress.
Altered mental status, lethargy, and orientation to person but not time or place.
Initial neurologic exam showed intact cranial nerves, normal gait, and no sensory or motor deficits.
She denied seizures and EEG monitoring did not reveal seizures.
Lumbar puncture showed lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein.
CSF white blood cell count was 127/uL.
CSF West Nile IgM by ELISA was 6.10 with normal less than 0.89.
CSF West Nile IgG by ELISA was 2.08 with normal less than 1.29.
Repeat MRI on hospital day 16 showed moderate periventricular white-matter changes.

time_series.source_text_value: Admission MRI showed no acute intracranial pathology.
Repeat MRI showed moderate periventricular white-matter changes.

imaging.source_text_value: CT brain on arrival revealed no evidence of acute intracranial pathology.

imaging.finding: No acute infarct or other intracranial pathology
imaging.source_text_value: Admission MRI revealed no acute infarct or other intracranial pathology.
MRI performed after clinical worsening showed moderate periventricular white-matter changes.

diagnostics.source_text_value: EEG monitoring did not reveal any seizures.
No pain on knee extension with hip flexed and no hip or knee flexion when head was lifted.

microbiology.source_text_value: West Nile CSF IgM was 6.10, above the reference range.
West Nile CSF IgG was 2.08, above the reference range.

microbiology.test: CSF Coccidioides antibody, Cryptococcus antigen, and VDRL
microbiology.source_text_value: Coccidioides antibody, Cryptococcus antigen, and VDRL were negative.

clinical_course_events.event: Presentation with fever, posterior headache, lethargy, and disorientation
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: Presented with altered mental status, fever, and headache of three days duration.

clinical_course_events.event: Clinical worsening with suspected facial droop and left-sided weakness
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: On hospital day 16, nursing staff reported facial droop and left-sided weakness; repeat MRI showed periventricular white-matter changes.
Clinical picture subsequently improved with continued supportive treatment.
At discharge she was alert and oriented, walking without issues, following commands, and answering appropriately.

outcome.neurologic_outcome: Improved during admission and discharged home alert, oriented, walking, following commands, and answering questions.
outcome.mortality_hazard_relevance: Moderate encephalitis with transient worsening and MRI evolution but no seizure, paralysis, respiratory failure, or death.

case_boundary_warnings: Do not use the normal admission MRI to exclude WNND; this case developed MRI white-matter abnormalities over about two weeks.
CSF West Nile IgM and compatible encephalitis are rankable pathogen evidence; Coccidioides, Cryptococcus, and VDRL negatives are preserved as non-ranking exclusion context.
EEG absence of seizure is preserved and should not be converted into absence of WNND.
